propositions.text: The appellant is a Tanzanian citizen appealing the RPD's denial of refugee protection.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX, (the Appellant) is a citizen of Tanzania. She appeals a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) denying her claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The appellant requests verification of a newspaper article and substitution by the RAD finding her a Convention Refugee or returning the matter to the RPD.
propositions.quote: The Appellant is asking for verification of the newspaper article, and a substitution by the RAD finding that the Appellant is a Convention Refugee, or alternatively returning the matter back to the RPD for redetermination.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant, a Tanzanian citizen, appeals the RPD's denial and requests newspaper verification and substitution or remand by the RAD.

propositions.text: The RAD refers the matter back to the RPD for re-determination by a differently-constituted panel under section 111(1)(c) IRPA.
propositions.quote: The RAD pursuant to section 111(1)(c) of the IRPA, refers the matter back to the Refugee Protection Division for re-determination by a differently-constituted panel.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD refers the matter back to the RPD for re-determination by a different panel under IRPA section 111(1)(c).

propositions.text: The appellant submitted a document on April 14, 2015, after the appeal was perfected and submitted.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submitted a document, on April 14, 2015, after the Appeal had been perfected and submitted.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submitted a document after the appeal was perfected and submitted on April 14, 2015.

propositions.text: Under Rule 29, the Division must consider relevance, probative value, new evidence, and whether the document could have been provided earlier.
propositions.quote: Evidence is submitted as part of a Rule 29 application. Under such an application, in addition to 110 (4), the rule requires that you consider the factors set out in Rule 29 (4). 29. (4) In deciding whether to allow an application, the Division must consider any relevant factors, including: (a) the documents relevance and probative value; (c) a new evidence the document brings to the appeal; and (c) whether the person who is subject of the appeal, with reasonable effort, could've provided the document or written submissions with the appellant's record, respondent's record, or reply record

paragraphs.summary: The court explains Rule 29 requires considering relevance, probative value, new evidence, and whether the document could have been provided earlier.

propositions.text: The new document verifies a newspaper page numbering error but is not probative or relevant to the RAD's decision.
propositions.quote: The document provided verifies that there was an error in the page numbering of the newspaper submitted in evidence and addressed by the RPD in its decision. ... The new evidence is not probative or relevant to the RAD's decision.

paragraphs.summary: The new document confirms a newspaper page numbering error but is not probative or relevant to the RAD's decision.

propositions.text: The RAD will address only one aspect of the Memorandum of Appeal in this decision.
propositions.quote: The RAD's decision, in this case, will deal with only one aspect of the Memorandum of appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD will address only one aspect of the Memorandum of Appeal in this decision.

propositions.text: The appellant alleges the RPD took and kept the original newspaper for authentication but did not authenticate it.
propositions.quote: The Appellant submits that the RPD took and kept the original of the newspaper for authentication purposes and does not seem to have authenticated the newspaper at all.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges the RPD kept the original newspaper but did not authenticate it.

propositions.text: The appellant alleges she is a lesbian with past relationships, forced marriage, daughters in Tanzania, attacks due to sexual orientation, and fled to Canada in 2014.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleges that she is a lesbian and has had a number of gay relationships with women in Tanzania. She alleges that in 1985 she was forced into marriage by her parents to XXXX XXXX who died in 1998. The Appellant has two daughters who are currently residing in Tanzania. The Appellant's most recent partner was XXXX XXXX by suspected Muslim fanatics in XXXX 2014 as a result of her sexual orientation. XXXX, the Appellant, was also attacked by these fanatics; she managed to escape the attack and went into hiding in XXXX, XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. In her last place of hiding, she met an agent to help facilitate her eventual flight to Canada. The Appellant came to Canada on XXXX XXXX, 2014 and made a refugee claim on the basis of her alleged sexual orientation on October 30, 2014.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant alleges lesbian orientation, forced marriage, attacks, hiding, and flight to Canada in 2014 to claim refugee protection.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the appellant's claim, finding no serious possibility of persecution or risk of torture or cruel treatment in Tanzania.
propositions.quote: In a decision of February 5, 2015 (January 29, 2015), the RPD rejected her claim finding that there is not a serious possibility that the Appellant would be persecuted in Tanzania, or that, on a balance of probabilities, she would be personally subjected to a danger of torture, or face a risk to her life, or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment in Tanzania.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the appellant's claim, finding no serious possibility of persecution or risk in Tanzania.

propositions.text: The appellant supports the Huruglica decision that the RAD should conduct a hybrid appeal and has not requested an oral hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellant supports the Huruglica,1 decision in that the RAD should conduct a hybrid appeal. The Appellant has not requested an oral hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant supports the Huruglica decision for a hybrid appeal and has not requested oral hearing.

propositions.text: The RAD must conduct a hybrid appeal reviewing all aspects and may substitute its own decision, respecting RPD credibility findings.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that Federal Court decision, in Huruglica,2 provides the RAD with guidance in relation to the appropriate standard that must be applied by a specialized tribunal, such as the RAD, to decisions of a first-level administrative tribunal. ... Justice Phelan states, in paragraphs 54 and 55, of the foregoing decision: [54] ... It must review all aspects of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment ... [55] ... it is not restricted, as an appellate court is, to intervening on facts only where there is an "overriding and palpable error."

paragraphs.summary: The RAD must conduct a hybrid appeal, independently assessing the RPD decision but respecting credibility findings.

propositions.text: The RAD will independently assess the RPD decision, affording deference to credibility findings where appropriate.
propositions.quote: Accordingly, the RAD will conduct its own assessment of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment of whether the Appellant is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection. Deference will be afforded to the credibility findings of the RPD or to other findings where the RPD has a particular advantage in reaching its conclusions.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD will independently assess the RPD decision, deferring to credibility findings where appropriate.

propositions.text: The RPD found the newspaper not credible due to picture mismatch and name error; the appellant said the picture was hers and name misspelled.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted several issues that caused it to find that the newspaper was not a credible evidence. The RPD noted that the picture in the newspaper did not resemble her and there was an error in her name. The Appellant testified that this was her picture and that they had made an error in spelling her first name, "XXXX" instead of "XXXX."

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the newspaper not credible due to picture and name errors; the appellant said the picture was hers and name misspelled.

propositions.text: The RPD observed inconsistent dates, fonts, page numbers, and color printing in the newspaper, leading to non-acceptance of its genuineness.
propositions.quote: The RPD made the following observations with respect to the newspaper: two different dates appeared, XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX, on the top right and left numbering of its pages, the font size, and the inconsistent type of the page numbers as well as the inconsistency of type throughout the newspaper articles. The RPD also noted that the front and back of the newspaper were printed in colour while the rest of the pages were printed in black and white. The Appellant gave an explanation for the different colourations in print, but had no explanation as to why the paper had two different dates. As a result of the RPD's observations, and on the overall credibility of the Appellant, the RPD did not accept the newspaper as genuine.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found inconsistent dates, fonts, page numbers, and color printing in the newspaper, rejecting its genuineness.

propositions.text: The appellant argues the RPD kept the original newspaper for authentication but no evidence shows verification was done.
propositions.quote: In the Appellant's appeal, she noted that the RPD kept the original of the newspaper for the purpose of authentication. There is no evidence or documentation in the file to indicate that this verification was done.

propositions.text: The appellant claims the newspaper is genuine and shows she was wanted by authorities in 2014; the RAD cannot support the RPD's decision on this.
propositions.quote: The basis of the Appellant's appeal is that the newspaper presented in evidence is genuine, and indicates that the Appellant was wanted by the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX 2014, the RAD is unable to support the RPD's decision on this issue.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the newspaper was not authenticated and is genuine, showing she was wanted; the RAD cannot support the RPD's decision.

propositions.text: The newspaper was not translated, preventing the RPD from making an informed decision on charges; CIC should have been contacted if charges were sufficient.
propositions.quote: The newspaper presented in evidence is critical to making the final determination in this decision. First, the newspaper was not translated so that it was impossible for the RPD to make an informed decision regarding the alleged charge, or charges. If the charges outlined were sufficient, Citizenship and Immigration Canada (CIC) should have been contacted in order to deal with the possibility of exclusion on 1(f)(b), or charges that would have supported her claim.

paragraphs.summary: The newspaper was untranslated, preventing informed RPD decision on charges; CIC should have been contacted if charges were sufficient.

propositions.text: The newspaper should have been authenticated; even if authenticated and translated, the RAD cannot substitute a decision due to its centrality to credibility.
propositions.quote: In that a major credibility issue is the RPD's finding that this newspaper was not genuine, the newspaper presented in evidence should have been sent for authentication. Even if the newspaper article had been translated and authenticated, the RAD would be unable to substitute a decision because the issue goes to the heart of the claim, and has an impact upon all other issues of the claim. Major determinations of the RPD regarding credibility are based on the lack of genuineness of the newspaper presented.

paragraphs.summary: The newspaper should have been authenticated; even if so, the RAD cannot substitute a decision due to its centrality to credibility.

propositions.text: The RAD will not make findings on other issues in the RPD decision or appellant's memorandum at this time.
propositions.quote: The RAD will not, at this time, make findings on the other issues written in the RPD's decision, and commented on by the Appellant in the Memorandum of Appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD will not make findings on other RPD decision issues or appellant's memorandum now.

propositions.text: The RAD refers the matter back to the RPD for re-determination by a differently-constituted panel under section 111(1)(c) IRPA.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to section 111(1)(c) of the IRPA, the RAD refers the matter back to the Refugee Protection Division for re-determination by a differently-constituted panel.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD refers the matter back to the RPD for re-determination by a different panel under IRPA section 111(1)(c).
